newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina's Siderar mulls $1 bln expansion - source.
newsitem.headline: Argentina's Siderar mulls $1 bln expansion - source.

text.p: Siderar SAIC, Argentina's largest steelmaker, is considering a plan to meet growing demand by investing $1 billion to boost its output, a company source said Thursday.
"We are considering a $1 billion plan to raise flat-steel output to 3.5 to four million tonnes a year, from 1.9 million, over the next four to five years," the source said.
"A decision will be taken towards the end of the year," the source said, confirming local press reports that quoted Siderar Chief Executive Javier Tizado.
Siderar, controlled by local holding company Techint, makes flat steel for cars, household appliances, building and food businesses, as well as tubes for pipelines.
Techint also controls Siderca. The company, together with Italy's Dalmine and Tubos de Acero de Mexico, forms an alliance that is a world leader in seamless steel tubes for the oil industry.
Techint posted $5.5 billion in revenues last year.
Siderar is considering the expansion in view of forecasts of strong economic growth and a subsequent rise in demand for steel products.
Siderar's sales in Argentina grew 20 percent in the first half of the year against the same period last year, the source said. "The priority is the domestic market."
The company posted revenues of $735 million in the nine months to March 31.

Siderar is currently facing a bottleneck that has hampered production. One of its two steel mills, two coking plants and a converter stand idle because the company lacks the capacity to process their output, the source said.
